title: FieldTwin candidate A: Nefud dune-bedrock margin, Ha'il region, Saudi Arabia
classification: under-recognized candidate / new proposed mission use (see docs/NOVELTY_AUDIT.md); NOT a first-ever claim

mission.task: Rehearse autonomous route planning and hazard avoidance across Jezero-like slope/relief, including a sand-to-bedrock transition (cf. Perseverance in sand-rich Seitah next to bedrock).

candidate.surface_visual_check: Crescentic dunes with interdune hollows; dark rock massif at SE corner (labelled 'Jabal al-Urfa - Jiran' on Google Maps). Checked by team on satellite imagery, 2026-11-15.

transfer_matrix.aspect: Slope distribution at 60 m (median about 5 deg, p90 about 11 deg)

transfer_matrix.evidence: visible in imagery; Jezero/Seitah has sand next to bedrock (NASA)
candidate 79 m vs Jezero median 272 m: inside the wide Jezero spread, but well below its median

transfer_matrix.aspect: Bedform scale (Nefud dunes tens of m vs Martian ripples about 1 m)
Surface material, grain size, bearing strength
transfer_matrix.evidence: quartz dune sand vs basaltic regolith; not measured
below DEM resolution; needs field survey or high-res imagery

field_test_protocol: 1. Lay out 3 route segments inside the 6 km window: dune-only, bedrock-only, and dune-to-bedrock crossing, with slope classes <5, 5-15 and 15-25 deg.
2. Run a stereo-vision autonomous navigation stack (AutoNav-like) with an emulated Earth-Mars command delay; log hazard detections.
3. Measure wheel slip vs slope on sand and on bedrock, path efficiency, localization drift, and hazard false positive/negative rates.
4. Repeat at two sun angles (low-texture dune faces are a documented vision failure mode, ESA Morocco 2018).
5. Report results against the Analog Transfer Matrix: sand strength and gravity effects must be corrected, not transferred.
